scope: 40 unchanged ordinary food primary assignments; existing tags retained and supplemental roles unassessed.
reviewedPrimaryRule: Own exact numeric-ID item state has Eat, equipable=No, and a full literal named-subject definition plus a subject-specific positive Hitpoints consumption mechanic. Prepared ordinary foods retain primary Food placement even when their source documents secondary recipe/quest uses. Mode-only copies require separate review.

reviewRecord: Root read all41 exact source definitions and eating/healing states, inspected competing full-page contexts and the special Eel sushi and delayed-healing hunter-meat paragraphs, and replayed the candidate builder. The40 ordinary IDs are approved only for their existing primary category/subcategory/tab; no numerical healing, tag, bankability or exhaustive secondary-role assertion is added to runtime data. A separate adversarial exact-state pass found no conflicting current-use condition among the40 ordinary IDs; raw source paragraphs, not normalized candidate renderings, supply the quoted healing evidence.

cases.title: Anchovies
cases.semanticExcerpt: '''Anchovies''' are a type of [[fish]] that restores 1 [[Hitpoints|Hitpoint]] when eaten. It can be obtained by cooking [[raw anchovies]] on a [[fire]] or [[cooking range]], granting 30 experience when successful. When cooking there is a chance to fail, resulting in [[burnt anchovies]]. The burn rate decreases as the player's [[Cooking]] level increases. Anchovies are one of a number of foods with a reduced burn rate while using the [[Cooking range (Lumbridge Castle)|Lumbridge Castle range]] with [[Cook's Assistant]] completed. It will stop burning entirely at Cooking level 34, or 31 when using the Lumbridge range.
